w: Swamishri arrived at Center Parcs at 7.50 pm for the 4-day Kishore - Kishori Shibir. The much awaited exciting and enlightening shibir was attended by 260 kishores and 220 kishoris.

In the opening session Swamishri said, "Kishore Mandal's Jay. I am very happy to see your love and enthusiasm. The venue of the shibir is very nice. You have to pass through a maze of buildings to get here. And you can get lost in the maze. You are all lost in the maze (of life) so you have to come out! We have come here to get you out. Do you understand?... Only one who knows the way can get you out of the maze. God and the holy Sadhu are our friends, relatives and well-wishers..." The 4-day shibir program from 27 to 30 June included videos, slide shows, narrations by kishores on 'Swami cares', explanations about murtis and holy relics in Swamishri's puja, 'Ruchi' quiz, question - answer session and sports.

Saanskrutik Virasat The evening Children’s Day special program was held at the Anaheim Convention Center. The LA Children’s forum presented ‘Sanskrutik Virasat’ which depicted the stories of Shravan, Dhruv and Nachiketa. Thereafter dignitaries honored Swamishri. Finally Swamishri said in his blessings, “Today nobody has any time, but they have time to go to parties. But one’s home is like a big party. Whatever wealth and name you may have achieved will be of no good if your children become corrupt, sinful and terrorists. So there is a need to be vigilant while raising children. You are vigilant in your business. So, too, you must be awakened in matters about raising your children. You should also listen to them with love and care…” The devotees and well-wishers appreciated the evening program.

At 8.25 pm the evening satsang assembly had concluded in the mandir. Swamishri was walking back to his room. On either side of his pathway devotees were standing for Swamishri’s darshan. On seeing a devotee Swamishri asked, “Piyush, are you well?” “Yes,” he replied. “Do you come to the mandir?” “Swami, I live 100 miles away.” “Let it be 100 miles away, but you can come to the mandir two to four times a month,” Swamishri emphasised. On seeing Swamishri’s insistence, Piyush tried to shunt the track of conversation, “Swami, I have pledged for some donations to the Atladra mandir. That donation…” Swamishri interrupted midway and said, “Listen to what I have to say! Do come to the mandir. And if the mandir is too far then you have a little mandir in your house. Come to this mandir once a month, but do the arti, puja, thal and home discourse at your home mandir every day. And be careful not to eat meat and fall into bad company. You must assemble all the family members and read satsang books, sing dhun and kirtans. By so doing your house will become a mandir.” For spiritual progress it is essential to engage ourselves in some spiritual endeavours on a daily basis. Otherwise, the material influences of society and our own base instincts dilute or annul our devotional feelings, faith and morals. Hence, Swamishri prescribes regular attendance to mandir, daily performance of devotional rituals and reading of scriptures.

Whenever his little grandson cried a local man of Bhadra would place a bidi in his mouth. Subsequently, the little child became addicted. Presently, he is three and a half years old and eats two packets of gutkha (tobacco) daily. When he does not get the gutkha he throws a tantrum. The boy's father and grandfather are addicted to gutkha and bidi.

Sometimes, the child goes all by himself to the local shop to get a gutkha under his father's name. The innocent, tender child has become habituated to tobacco all because of his father and grandfather's mistake.

The child's uncle, who is a devotee and lives in Surat, brought him for Swamishri’s darshan. He placed him on the rostrum. Swamishri welcomed him, “Jai Swaminarayan.” But the ignorant little child did not know what to say. He simply looked down and remained quiet. Swamishri asked for a box of prasad, and taking a sweet ball from it, said, “Take this, and don't eat gutkha. Gutkha spoils your body and causes disease. Therefore don't eat it.”
Swamishri's compassion for the little, tender child was apparent to all. To release him from the shackles of addiction Swamishri blessed him and advised him and his relatives.

Every year the city of Amdavad celebrates the popular festival of Rath Yatra with pomp and joy. The murtis of Bhagwan Shri Jagannath, Balaram and Subhadra are ceremoniously carried in floats from the Jagannath Mandir through the streets of Amdavad all day.

The Rath Yatra festival was also celebrated by Swamishri at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Amdavad. Swamishri arrived for Thakorji’s darshan at 7.20 am. A golf cart was transformed into a decorated rath. Swamishri performed pujan of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Bhagwan Jagannath. Thereafter Swamishri sat in the rath and performed five pradakshinas of the mandir. In the lead were dancing children dressed in traditional clothes. Then sadhus followed, singing bhajans and charging the air with devotion and festivity. Behind Swamishri’s rath were many leading devotees. And all around the festive path thousands of devotees were singing and joyfully absorbing the festive darshan. In conclusion, Swamishri’s chariot was steered into the main auditorium. The singing and dancing by children and youths made the occasion devotional and divine. Swamishri was seated with folded hands, blessing the devotees as the rath proceeded towards the stage.

During Swamishri’s puja sadhus sang bhajans on the rath yatra festival. Thereafter Swamishri performed pujan and arti of Maharaj’s murti. In the evening assembly Swamishri steered Shri Harikrishna Maharaj on a small rath with a remote control console. Thereafter in his blessings he said, “Man loves festivals. Shriji Maharaj celebrated festivals. Though he was God, he celebrated Janmashtmi, Ram Navmi, Rath Yatra and other festivals. He added the elements of spiritual discourses and bhajans so that one could strike a rapport with God. Maharaj reformed the prevailing gatherings into festivals of devotion, worship and wisdom.”

During Swamishri's walk, 'Yagnapurush Charitam' was being read. It came to where Shastriji Maharaj crossed the Radhu river sitting in a tub. So Yogicharan Swami asked Swamishri, "Did Shastriji Maharaj know how to swim?"
"No. Neither he nor Yogiji Maharaj could." Saying this, he added firmly, "They may not have known how to swim, but both he and Yogiji Maharaj have carried us across (the ocean of the world)."
